newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says considering extra corporate taxes.
newsitem.headline: France says considering extra corporate taxes.

text.p: France's Socialist government is studying the possibility of additional taxes on company profits if extra efforts are needed to finance social measures and spur economic growth, government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said on Wednesday.

"The prime minister recalled that if efforts are needed to promote solidarity and to contribute to economic recovery, then they should be shared by the different players in the economy -- public ones but also companies," she said after a weekly cabinet meeting.
"We are looking at the possibility of calling for an extra effort from companies and this would be made by companies which are profitable," she told a news conference.

Trautmann said the issue had not however been discussed at the cabinet meeting itself, adding that any decision would have to take account of the results of an audit of public finances due on July 21.
France's new Socialist party leader Francois Hollande said earier on Tuesday that if extra budgetary measures were needed these would not fall on households but on profitable companies.
